dispatch.return_contract: eax = edi: 1 = target was OPENED (was hidden); 0 = target was CLOSED or id invalid (ids 5/10 and >0xF jump straight to the shared tail 0x42B3DD with edi=0 from the prologue xor). Callers rely on this: Q/W/E/R/S/D/N/G letters, Enter case1, FnB 0x43E4B0 notice path, caption action stubs (cap14 toggles only when return 0, cap15 double-toggle gates on return).
dispatch.close_all_first: 0x0042B820 demote-all runs before the case: walks the visible list from [base+0xD28] head via node+4 (prev links), resets [base+0xD34]=0 and per listed node id <= 0xE executes table 0x42B938 -> 0x423F90(subwin, 0) (mov [subwin+0x34],0; ret 4); ids 5/10 -> 0x42B8F5 no-op advance, id > 0xE skipped; loop inc edi / cmp edi,[base+0xD38] / jl. This is DEACTIVATION of the +0x34 slot only - it does NOT touch the +0x30 visibility gate and does NOT unlink list nodes. 3 E8 callers: 0x42ADB6 (dispatcher head), 0x42B6B3 (drag-start 0x42B6A0), 0x42BD8F (FnA hit-test fallback).
dispatch.case_pattern: mov eax,[esi+flagoff]; push id; test eax,eax; mov ecx,esi; je OPEN; call 0x0042AC50; vtable[0x10](0); xor edi,edi; ret | OPEN: call 0x0042AC30; vtable[0x10](1); [per-id specials]; mov edi,1; ret. flagoff = objectoff + 0x30 in every case (see records).
dispatch.state_gate_expression: window_object+0x30 - each case tests [base+flagoff] where flagoff = objectoff+0x30 (record state_gate fields; e.g. id0 object base+0x6554, gate base+0x6584 = +0x30). The +0x30 slot is written by the class visibility setter 0x0043F020 -> 0x00423F80 (mov [obj+0x30],arg; ret 4; sole caller 0x43F033; also sets [obj+0x274]) and read by draw paths (e.g. 0x43F04A gates paint on [obj+0x30]); the toggle dispatcher itself never writes it - the vtable[0x10] callback does. Distinct from the +0x34 active slot written by 0x00423F90 (demote-all 0x42B820 / drag-start 0x42B6A0) and the +0x3C gate required by drag math.
dispatch.show_helper_proof: 0x0042AC30 adds main+0xD24 to the list manager and calls 0x00449870, which allocates/inserts a node containing the requested window ID.
dispatch.hide_helper_proof: 0x0042AC50 walks the main+0xD28 linked list, unlinks the matching ID node, decrements the count and releases it through 0x004680F8.

insertion_policy.empty_list: The new node initializes the circular head/tail links and becomes both manager+0x04 and manager+0x0C.
insertion_policy.nonempty_list: The new node is linked after the current manager+0x0C tail; manager+0x0C is advanced to the new node and count manager+0x14 is incremented.
insertion_policy.paint_order_implication: 0x004280F0 starts from manager+0x04 and follows node+0x04, so a newly shown window is appended to the visible paint sequence and is later in the sequence than already-visible windows.
insertion_policy.hide_behavior: 0x0042AC50 unlinks the matching node, decrements manager+0xD38 and releases it through 0x004680F8; showing it again appends a fresh node.

caller_scan.promotion_result: The recovered command paths show ordinary open actions call the dispatcher once with the target ID; the corresponding cleanup paths are separate. No direct hide-then-show pair was found in the same basic block. A later open can still append a window after a prior cleanup, but an unconditional top-level promotion policy is not proven.

notice_id15_caller_resolution.result: ID15 is shown after the independent notice/result preparation call succeeds; this evidence does not bind it exclusively to the guild page.

interpretation: The original UI has a separate visibility state machine from its position-update dispatcher. A window object is tested at its +0x30 state gate; showing registers its window ID in the main+0xD24 linked-list manager, while hiding removes that ID node. The virtual +0x10 callback then receives 1/0. Shared construction and the main-init call scan now prove the default gate is zero and registration alone does not make a window visible.
